topic: fractions as numbers: correcting models with unequal parts

problems.desc: Answer must say that a fraction names EQUAL parts: the circle's three parts are not the same size, so one of three unequal parts cannot be called one third. Accept any wording that identifies the unequal parts as the reason.
Rectangle A must be circled. The explanation must say that only the rectangle cut into equal-size parts truly shows one fourth; the other rectangle's parts are different sizes.

traps.desc: counted 1 of the 3 unequal parts and called it one third instead of counting equal squares

problems.desc: The mistake named must be that the three parts are not equal in size, so counting 1 part out of 3 does not give a fraction; the equal small squares must be counted instead.
The explanation must say the tick marks were not evenly spaced, so the pieces of the line are not equal fourths; marks for fourths must cut the line into equal lengths.
Answer must be no: halves must be equal parts, and 12 cm is not the same length as 8 cm, so neither part is one half of the strip.

traps.desc: counted 1 section out of 4 unequal sections and called it one fourth

problems.desc: The explanation must say the four sections are not equal in size, so 1 section out of 4 is not one fourth of the garden; the equal small squares show the true share.
The drawing must cut the grid into six parts of equal size (each covering the same number of small squares) with exactly one part shaded; parts may have different shapes.
